q: How does the Vedral-Barenco-Ekert ripple adder compare quantitatively to modern quantum arithmetic primitives (Draper QFT adder, Cuccaro ripple adder, Gidney's carry-lookahead) in gate count, T-count, and circuit depth at n=8, 16, 32?
basis: The 1996 paper predates the Draper (2000) and Cuccaro (2004) constructions. We reproduced VBE's 8n+O(1) gate scaling with R^2=1.0 but never compared it head-to-head against the more modern primitives that are now the default in Q# / Qiskit / Cirq. Rick's rule requires a genuine comparison probe.
next_steps: Implement Cuccaro and Draper adders under the same gate/qubit accounting (NOT/CNOT/Toffoli decomposition, temp-reset check), run gate counts and depth on n in {4,8,16,32}, and report gate-count, T-count (after Toffoli->T decomposition), and depth ratios vs the VBE baseline in this replication. All local, no external endpoint required.

q: Does the VBE modular exponentiation, when scaled to cryptographic sizes (e.g., n=1024 or n=2048 for RSA-scale factoring), still respect the 7n+1 to 4n+3 memory formula without hitting compilation blowups from Toffoli-to-Clifford+T decomposition?
basis: We verified 7n+1, 5n+2, 4n+3 numerically for N in {15,21,35} (n <= 6) and reproduced the 'about 20 ions for N=15' figure exactly. We did NOT probe whether the formulas remain tight after fault-tolerant compilation, which is where the qubit budget actually lives for Shor-scale factoring.
next_steps: Symbolically evaluate 7n+1 / 5n+2 / 4n+3 for n in {512, 1024, 2048}; then compile the mod-adder to a Clifford+T circuit (Toffoli -> 7 T + 8 Clifford) and report ancilla overhead and T-count for one representative sub-block. Free tooling: Qiskit or pyLIQUi via local install.

q: Under a T-count / T-depth cost model (the relevant metric for fault-tolerant quantum computers), is the VBE adder still competitive with Draper/Cuccaro, or is the 8n Toffoli count a hidden cost that the paper's asymptotic gate-count hides?
basis: The paper predates the modern insight that T-gates dominate the cost of fault-tolerant quantum arithmetic. Our replication reports Toffoli+CNOT counts (matching the paper's accounting), but did not attempt Toffoli -> {T, Clifford} decomposition, which is what actually matters for a 2026 quantum computer.
next_steps: Decompose one full VBE adder block at n=8 into Clifford+T using the standard 7T-per-Toffoli decomposition, count T-gates and T-depth, and compare against Cuccaro (which has a known T-count of ~14n) and Draper (which trades T for depth). Local computation, free.

q: Can an ML-driven synthesis tool (e.g., reinforcement-learning circuit optimization, or a genetic-algorithm ancilla-reduction pass) find a lower-gate-count reversible modular adder for a fixed N (say N=15 or N=21) than the VBE Fig.-4 construction?
basis: The paper hand-crafts the mod-adder as add-a, subtract-N, overflow-detect, conditional add-back, temp reset. This is provably correct but not proved optimal. No modern ML-driven arithmetic-circuit synthesis pass has been run against these specific low-n mod-adder instances in the replication.
next_steps: Take VBE mod-adder at n=4 (N=15), enumerate all functionally-equivalent {Toffoli, CNOT} circuits up to depth 30 via a bounded SAT / RL search, and report whether any construction beats VBE's gate count while preserving the temp-reset invariant. Local, free.

q: Does the exhaustive basis-state validation we ran (n <= 4 for plain adder, N <= 15 for mod-adder) extrapolate to a proof of correctness at larger n, or is there a known family of edge cases (e.g., all-ones inputs, near-N inputs) where implementation mistakes would only surface at n >= 8?
basis: We only verified n in {2,3,4}. The VBE construction is inductive on n so correctness at n=4 morally implies correctness at n=8, but we did not run an SMT-based proof of the parameterized adder circuit, and we did not target the worst-case inputs (a=N-1, b=N-1) at higher n where carry chains are longest.
next_steps: Run targeted large-n sweeps at n in {8, 12} covering only worst-case inputs (a=b=N-1, a=0/b=N-1, a=N/2/b=N/2), and separately encode the parameterized VBE adder as an SMT formula (Z3) to attempt a symbolic-n correctness proof for at least the CARRY/SUM primitives. Local, free.
